title: Macrophage ILF3 promotes abdominal aortic aneurysm by inducing inflammatory imbalance in male mice

predicted_errors.error_location: Results – AAA overexpression section (Fig. 2) and AAA deficiency section (Fig. 3)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The conditional overexpression strain is defined as "ILF3 conditional overexpression mice (ILF3^flox/floxLysMCre^+; hereafter referred to as ILF3^M–Tg)", while the knockout strain is defined with the identical genotype: "macrophage-ILF3 knockout mice (ILF3^flox/floxLysMCre^+; hereafter referred to as ILF3^M–KO)". The same allele/Cre combination cannot simultaneously generate macrophage ILF3 overexpression and macrophage ILF3 deletion; the genotype description for at least one of the two lines is wrong (an overexpression line would require e.g. a LSL-ILF3 knock-in allele).

predicted_errors.error_location: Results, paragraph describing Fig. 4C/4D (inflammatory mediators in vivo)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states "the expression of several inflammatory cytokines and chemokines, including monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 (MCP-1), IL-6, TNF-α, and IL-10 exhibited a pronounced decrement in the ILF3^M-KO ApoE–/– mice" and that these "were significantly upregulated in the ILF3^M-Tg ApoE–/– group", yet two sentences later asserts "the macrophage-produced immunosuppressive cytokine IL-10 expression was diametrically opposed to the aforementioned pro-inflammatory mediators". It also contradicts the in vitro data in the preceding paragraph ("IL-10 levels were, however, intensified due to the lack of ILF3"). IL-10 cannot be both decreased and oppositely regulated in ILF3-deficient mice.

predicted_errors.error_location: Results, end of Fig. 5 mechanism paragraph ('Collectively, these findings indicate...')
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The sentence "ILF3 deficiency modulates inflammatory balance by simultaneously inhibiting the NF-κB and Keap1-Nrf2 signaling pathways" contradicts both the data reported immediately before it (decreased Keap1, restored Nrf2 nuclear translocation, "elevated Nrf2-ARE DNA binding in ILF3-deficient macrophages") and the later summary of the same experiments ("ILF3 deficiency modulates inflammatory balance through dual mechanisms: inhibiting NF-κB via p105 upregulation and activating Keap1-Nrf2 pathway due to reduced Keap1 expression"). ILF3 deficiency activates, not inhibits, Nrf2 signaling.

predicted_errors.error_location: Fig. 1J legend vs. Results (single-cell analysis paragraph)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states cells were clustered and visualized "Through UMAP and canonical markers" (Supplementary Figs. 1D, E), but the Fig. 1J legend states "ILF3⁺ macrophages from human AAA and non-aneurysmal samples were projected onto the t-SNE plot". The same single-cell dataset cannot be described with two different dimensionality-reduction embeddings without explanation.

For a per-cell feature plot the legend states "The color intensity of each dot corresponds to the average gene expression across all cells" — this description belongs to the dot-plot (panel K, where color = average expression) and is incorrect for a t-SNE/UMAP feature plot in which each dot is a single cell and color encodes that cell's expression.

The same-named control group with the same sample size gives two different mortality figures: "mortality rate of ILF3^M–WT ApoE^–/– (37.50%, 12/32; Fig. 2D)" and "the mortality rate of ILF3^M-WT ApoE^-/- mice post-Ang II infusion was 40.63% (13/32)" (Fig. 3D). If these are the same littermate control cohort (identical genotype label and n = 32), the numbers are mutually inconsistent; if they are different cohorts this is not stated anywhere.

predicted_errors.error_location: Results, end of in vitro macrophage paragraph (Fig. 4E, Supplementary Fig. 5C)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paragraph reports only immunoblotting of cytokines in ILF3-deficient macrophages, yet concludes "deficiency of macrophage-derived ILF3 attenuates Ang-II-induced inflammatory cell infiltration and concomitant inflammation, while an elevation in ILF3 expression exerts the opposite effect." No infiltration measurement and no ILF3-overexpressing macrophage data are presented in the cited panels, so the conclusion exceeds the evidence provided (the infiltration data are only introduced in the subsequent paragraph).

The legend states "Data are represented as mean ± SD" and then, for the same panels, "Boxplots were created using the first and third quartiles... (1E–1F, 1H–1I and 1L)". The same panels cannot simultaneously display mean ± SD bars and quartile-based boxplots; the descriptive-statistics description is internally inconsistent.

The paper states ILF3 mediates "enhanced vascular smooth muscle cell apoptosis due to the overexpression of circACTA2 via reducing CDK4 mRNA stability". The published circACTA2–ILF3 work describes ILF3 binding that stabilizes CDK4 mRNA and promotes VSMC proliferation, so both the direction of the effect on CDK4 mRNA stability and the cellular outcome appear misrepresented.
